learning_objective: 🎯 Learn to create engaging, multimedia-rich slides to present information effectively to an audience, using layouts, animations, and transitions.

key_vocabulary.definition: A systematic display of information using a sequence of slides.
A single page or screen in a digital presentation.
The visual effect that occurs when moving from one slide to the next during a presentation.
Visual effects applied to individual objects (text, images) INSIDE a single slide.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Software like MS PowerPoint or LibreOffice Impress helps you present ideas visually. A presentation consists of multiple slides. The 'Slide Sorter View' lets you see all slides at once to easily rearrange them, while 'Normal View' is used for editing.

A layout defines how text boxes and images are arranged (e.g., Title Slide, Two Content). The 'Slide Master' is the top-level blueprint; if you add a school logo to the Slide Master, it automatically appears on every single slide in the presentation.

This is a critical distinction! **Transitions** happen BETWEEN slides (e.g., Slide 1 fades out, Slide 2 slides in). **Animations** happen ON the slide (e.g., Bullet point 1 flies in, then an image bounces in).

Press F5 (usually) to start the Slide Show in full screen from the beginning. You can advance slides by clicking the mouse, using arrow keys, or setting automatic timers. Presenter guidelines: use less text (bullet points), clear fonts, and high-contrast colors.

fun_activity.title: ✨ Death by Powerpoint
fun_activity.instructions: A bad presentation has 500 words on a slide, yellow text on a white background, and every word spinning and bouncing with laser sound effects. This distracts the audience! The golden rule of presentations is 'KISS' - Keep It Short & Simple. The slides are meant to support you, not replace you!

exam_tips: 📌 The difference between Transition and Animation is a highly repeated exam question. Memorize the definitions clearly.
📌 'Slide Master' is used for consistency. Any formatting done on the master applies to all slides instantly.
📌 Remember standard shortcut keys: F5 starts the presentation from the beginning; Shift+F5 starts from the current slide.
quick_recap: ⭐ The 'Title Slide' is typically the first slide that introduces the topic and the presenter.
⭐ You can insert Audio and Video files into slides to make presentations truly multimedia.
⭐ Notes Page View allows the presenter to type private speaking notes that the audience won't see on the projector.
